final:
All 4 of the reviewer's issues are accurate. I wrote the verdicts to `verdicts.json` and made no code changes.

| Verdict | Count |
|---|---|
| Valid, should fix | 3 (#1, #2, #3) |
| Valid, optional | 1 (#0) |

The PR made `getCalendar` async (`packages/app-store/_utils/getCalendar.ts:9`), so callers now have to wait for it. In several places they do that inside `forEach(async ...)`. `forEach` throws away the promises the callback returns, so nothing ever waits for the calendar or video deletions.

- **#0, `handleCancelBooking.ts:458-470`** (correctness): Valid, optional.
  - The callback adds results to `apiDeletes` only after its own awaits finish. By then line 652 has already run `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))`, so these recurring-event deletions are never awaited.
  - This `forEach(async ...)` was already there before the PR. The PR only added `await getCalendar` inside it.
  - The PR already switched the neighbouring else-branch (lines 477-483) to a `for...of` loop, so doing the same here would be easy and consistent.
- **#1, `wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts:125`, and #2, `vital/lib/reschedule.ts:125`** (correctness): Valid, should fix.
  - The PR turned these callbacks into `forEach(async ...)`.
  - The surrounding try/catch no longer catches anything. If `getCalendar` fails while loading the app, the error goes unhandled, where before the PR it would have been caught.
  - The deletions weren't awaited before the PR either. Still, the fix is a one-liner: `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))`.
- **#3, `trpc/.../bookings.tsx:553-567`** (correctness): Valid, should fix.
  - It's the same pattern. The handler moves straight on to sending the reschedule email and webhooks without waiting for the deletions.
  - There's no try/catch here, so any failure goes unhandled. The fix is the same as #1 and #2.

In every case the "deletions aren't awaited" part partly existed before this PR. What the PR adds is the async callback, which also lets errors from the new async `getCalendar` call go uncaught. So these are real issues, but I'd fix them as low-risk cleanups rather than urgent bugs.
